Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1123 AM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 241630Z - 251200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM CENTRAL NORTH
DAKOTA INTO NORTHERN MINNESOTA...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of large to very large hail, damaging
winds, and a tornado risk are expected this afternoon and evening
across portions of North Dakota into northern Minnesota.

...Dakotas/northern Minnesota...
Visible-satellite imagery late this morning shows a thin stratus
shield across central into northern MN ahead of a cluster of
thunderstorms over southern Manitoba.  This thunderstorm activity is
associated with a weak mid-level vorticity max embedded within an
amplifying northwest-flow pattern over the Upper Midwest.  A surface
trough extends southwestward into ND from a cyclone moving east
along the south shore of Hudson Bay.  

A plume of relatively steep mid-level lapse rates will overspread a
warm and moist boundary layer along/east of the surface trough, with
MLCAPE increasing above 2000 J/kg across parts of North Dakota into
northern Minnesota by late afternoon.  Forecast model soundings show
elongated hodographs thereby promoting storm organization, including
supercells and eventually a small cluster or two.  Morning models
continue to indicate widely scattered (ND) to scattered storm
development (MN) later this afternoon into the evening.  Large to
very large hail is possible with the supercells (1 to 3 inches in
diameter).  Some tornado risk will likely focus across northern MN
where lower temperature-dewpoint spreads and enlarged hodographs
become co-located for a few hours.  Any organized clustering could
result in localized corridors of greater severe-wind potential. 
Some severe threat could persist as storms move into a larger
portion of northern/central Minnesota through late evening, with a
general weakening trend expected overnight due to increasing CINH
and weakening buoyancy. 

Farther northwest, some guidance depicts isolated supercell
development west of the surface trough across the Canadian Prairies
during the late afternoon, which could then move into parts of
northern/central North Dakota within a northwesterly flow regime. 

...Eastern ID into northeast NV...
A weak disturbance evident in water-vapor imagery will continue to
move northeast over northern UT into southeast ID this afternoon
along the periphery of the Four Corners upper ridge.  Widely
scattered high-based storms will likely develop by late afternoon. 
Forecast soundings show inverted-V profiles supporting ample
evaporative cooling with the stronger downdrafts.  Isolated severe
gusts 60-70 mph are possible.

...Southern High Plains vicinity...
On the western periphery of residual early day precipitation/cloud
cover, a nearly stationary front draped from eastern New Mexico into
the Texas Panhandles is expected to become a focus for thunderstorm
development by late afternoon and early evening. While deep-layer
winds will be weak, strong boundary-layer heating/mixing will
support potential for localized downbursts. 

...Southeast AZ...
Isolated to widely scattered storms are forecast to develop late
this afternoon and slowly propagate westward.  A couple of the
stronger high-based downdrafts may yield a risk for severe gusts for
a few hours before this activity dissipates by late evening. 

...Coastal Carolinas...
Near/south of a residual front, relatively strong heating of a
moisture-rich airmass will result in the development of moderate
buoyancy across the Carolina coastal plain.  Scattered storm
development is expected by early/mid afternoon.  A couple of
stronger water-loaded downdrafts may be capable of a localized
wind-damage risk.

..Smith/Moore.. 07/24/2026

Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1233 PM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 251200Z - 261200Z

...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ROM THE 
NORTHERN ROCKIES INTO THE UPPER MIDWEST...AND ACROSS PORTIONS OF
SOUTHEAST ARIZONA...

...SUMMARY...
Isolated severe storms will be possible from the northern Rockies
into the upper Midwest, and across portions of southeast Arizona.

...Synopsis...
A belt of enhanced mid-level flow will move around the northern
periphery of the high amplitude ridge across the central US
D2/Saturday. Southwesterly mid-level flow will overspread portions
of the northern Rockies, with more northwesterly flow shifting
across the Upper Midwest into the Great Lakes Region.  At the
surface, a weak front will extend from a surface low over the
northern and central Plains to the Southeast coastal areas. 

...Northern Rockies...
Deeply mixed boundary layer conditions are expected across the
Northern Rockies amid dry sub-cloud inverted-v soundings and steep
low to mid level lapse rates. Scattered afternoon thunderstorm
development is expected across the high terrain. Moderate
instability is progged along with strong deep layer shear, which may
support isolated stronger cells with potential for strong to severe
wind gusts.

...South Dakota and the Upper Midwest to the Great Lakes...
Strong daytime heating is expected across the northern Plains into
the Upper Midwest and Great Lakes Region. Daytime temperatures are
progged to possibly exceed 100 F south of the weak front from the
Dakotas into the Upper Midwest. With the building high amplitude
ridge, warming around the 850-700 mb level will result in capping
across much of the more strongly unstable air mass. It does appear
that portions of northern/central Minnesota into northern Wisconsin
and the Upper Peninsula of Michigan may see enough weakening of the
cap to allow for isolated thunderstorm development by the afternoon.
Forecast soundings suggest veering wind profiles favorable for
supercells. Strong deep layer shear and linearly elongated profiles
will support large to very large hail and damaging wind. Though
low-level shear is more marginal, low tornado potential will exist.

Additional isolated thunderstorms may develop near the Black Hills
in South Dakota. Very hot and moderately unstable conditions are
expected amid steep low to mid-level lapse rates. Isolated
supercells capable of large hail and damaging wind will be possible,
with potential for some clustering downstream and increase in
damaging wind potential into the evening. 

...Southeast Arizona...
The favorable position of the surface high across the Four Corners
will bring moist easterly flow across southeastern Arizona. Some
enhancement of the easterly flow will allow for modest shear
profiles. It is likely that storms will develop across the high
terrain and move into the low deserts through the afternoon/evening.
Deeply mixed profiles and modest shear for organization will support
potential for strong to severe winds.

..Thornton.. 07/24/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0207 AM CDT Fri Jul 24 2026

Valid 261200Z - 271200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS OVER THE UPPER
MISSISSIPPI VALLEY INTO UPPER MIDWEST...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms capable of mainly large hail and damaging winds
are possible from the upper Mississippi Valley and Great Lakes into
portions of the Ohio and mid Missouri Valleys on Sunday and Sunday
night.

...Synopsis...
Along the periphery of an upper high anchored over the central and
southern Plains, a belt of enhanced mid-level winds will extend from
the Pacific Northwest through south-central Canada into the Great
Lakes. A series of perturbations will be embedded within the
higher-momentum flow regime, the most notable being a disturbance
tracking through southern parts of SK and MB into northwest ON and
northern MN late Sunday night. A surface low is forecast to follow
that same track with an associated trough or weak cool front
advancing through the northern Plains into the upper MS Valley.


...Upper Mississippi Valley into the Great Lakes...
Boundary-layer dewpoints in the 60s to mid 70s will coincide with an
eastward-expanding EML plume and associated cap to yield a fairly
widespread reservoir of moderate to strong instability across the
region on Sunday. There is some model signal for a subtle mid-level
disturbance to progress from the northern Plains into the upper
Midwest during the day with an associated band of forcing for ascent
potentially serving as a focus for diurnally enhanced thunderstorm
development. However, the absence of discernible surface boundaries
and the residual capping leads to uncertainty in the location and
extent of diurnally enhanced thunderstorm development. Nonetheless,
a conditional severe weather threat will exist with any storms that
can become rooted within the boundary layer, given the presence of
35-50 kt deep-layer shear.

More substantial forcing for ascent is forecast Sunday evening into
night across the upper MS Valley with the approach of the mid-level
wave mentioned in the synopsis. At that time, the surface front will
be moving into the area from the west, potentially serving as a
focus for thunderstorm development. The 00Z ECMWF in particular
depicts a large thunderstorm complex developing over that area with
a subsequent southward movement toward the mid MO Valley Sunday
night into early Monday. A corridor of enhanced damaging wind
potential would exist in that scenario; however, confidence in such
an occurrence is presently too low to include higher probabilities
and a conditional intensity group 1 contour.

..Mead.. 07/24/2026
